newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BEEZER BLANKS RANGERS AS PANTHERS WIN PLAYOFF OPENER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BEEZER BLANKS RANGERS AS PANTHERS WIN PLAYOFF OPENER.

text.p: John Vanbiesbrouck recaptured the form that carried the Panthers all the way to the Stanley Cup Finals last year as Florida blanked the New York Rangers 3-0 in their NHL playoff opener on Thursday.

Four first-round, best-of-seven Eastern Conference playoff series began Thursday with the home team -- Florida, New Jersey, Philadelphia and Buffalo -- striking first blood in each one in the hunt for Lord Stanley's Cup.

In Miami, Vanbiesbrouck stopped all 34 shots he faced to shut out his former team and Johan Garpenlov, Kirk Muller and Rob Niedermayer scored in the second period as Florida took the first small step back to the finals.
Robert Svehla assisted on all three Florida goals.
Vanbiesbrouck, a Ranger from 1981-1993, was playing New York in the playoffs for the first time and notched his fourth career post-season shutout with some help from his goal posts.
"(Alexander) Karpovtsev hit the post in the first, (Brian) Leetch hit the post in the second and when you get those kinds of breaks you begin to think it's meant to be," he said.
The Panthers were able to play their tight-checking defensive style most of the way and when the Rangers did break loose, Vanbiesbrouck was there to thwart them.
"We played our system, we were patient and Beezer was great," said Panthers coach Don MacLean.
The Rangers were unable to muster a shot during a 1:45 two-man advantage in the third period.
"Five-on-threes, you've got to score 95 percent of the time," said frustrated New York captain Mark Messier. "Vanbiesbrouck had a heck of a game."

At New Jersey, Brian Rolston scored twice and Martin Brodeur became the second goaltender in playoff history to score a goal as the Devils dominated the third period for a 5-2 victory over the Montreal Canadiens.
The Devils survived a nearly disastrous second period when their defensive trapping style broke down in the face of Montreal's superior speed.
New Jersey gave up short-handed goals to Shayne Corson and Benoit Brunet in the second period as well as a number of odd-man rushes that Brodeur had to deal with.
But the Devils bounced back in the third as Bill Guerin broke a 2-2 tie with 14:41 remaining and Rolston added a short-handed insurance goal with 8:01 to go for his second of the night.
Brodeur, who made 28 saves, capped the scoring with an empty net goal with 45 seconds left, joining Philadelphia's Ron Hextall as the only goalies ever to score in the playoffs.

"It's unbelievable, it's a great feeling," said Brodeur, who retrieved a loose puck from behind his goal and flipped the it high into the air. The puck bounced at mid ice and skittered into the vacant Montreal goal. "I put a lot on it. I was trying to score," Brodeur said with a huge grin.
In Philadelphia, Eric Lindros scored one goal and set up three more and Garth Snow stopped 27 shots for his first playoff win as the Flyers skated to a 5-1 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Pat Falloon scored twice, Rod Brind'Amour had a goal and an assist and John LeClair also tallied for Philadelphia, which outmuscled the Penguins all night.
Jaromir Jagr scored the lone Pittsburgh goal as Mario Lemieux, playing what could be the final playoff series of his brilliant career, was held without a point.
It was just the 13th time that Lemieux, who plans to retire at the end of this season, was held pointless in 85 career playoff games.
The Flyers converted two of four powerplay chances while holding the Penguins scoreless on three man-advantage situations.
"I thought we played well," Lindros said. "Winning the first game at home is so important. Last year we lost to Florida in the Spectrum and we never recovered from it."

In Buffalo, Brian Holzinger had a short-handed goal and set up a late third-period insurance tally and Dominik Hasek turned aside 22 shots as the Sabres beat the Senators 3-1, spoiling Ottawa's post-season debut.
Derek Plante and Randy Burridge also scored for the Sabres, who managed just five shots against Ottawa goaltender Ron Tugnutt in the third period but scored twice.
After being held at bay by Hasek over the first two periods, the Senators finally broke through on Daniel Alfredsson's powerplay goal 3:57 into the third.
With Buffalo defenceman Richard Smehlik all over him, Alfredsson tapped a loose rebound of an Alexei Yashin shot between Hasek's pads for Ottawa first-ever post-season goal.
But the Sabres rallied as Plante took a pass from Brad May and beat Tugnutt on a breakaway just 71 seconds later to snap the 1-1 tie.
"To capitalise at that time was big for our team," said Plante. "We got a couple of goals at the end. Basically both teams were just fighting it out the whole game."
